independentChallenges.case: Abort before source COMMIT; crash after acknowledged COMMIT but before wakeup; lose source COMMIT acknowledgement while mutation plus intent may have committed.
independentChallenges.assessment: Rollback exposes neither mutation nor intent. Restart discovers the committed immutable intent. Lost COMMIT acknowledgement follows TX-001 unknown classification and cannot blindly rerun the source action; source-operation/revision uniqueness prevents replacement identity.

independentChallenges.case: A claims generation n, pauses before possible_dispatch, and B reclaims generation n+1. A resumes and tries to send. Also expire A's lease without yet running B.
independentChallenges.assessment: A must successfully commit fenced dispatch admission before HTTP. A stale generation cannot checkpoint and therefore cannot send. Current generation alone is not sufficient authority after its bounded lease expires: admission must still have a valid database-time claim and remaining execution budget. The finite-lease owner decision supplies this constraint; the SQL predicate is future adapter work, not a new owner choice.
independentChallenges.disposition: sound_at_contract_level; require zero stale/expired-worker dispatches in implementation conformance

independentChallenges.case: A commits possible_dispatch and crashes either before any socket bytes or after provider acceptance; lease expires and B attempts recovery.
independentChallenges.assessment: Both crashes remain unknown without trusted outcome evidence. B cannot dispatch again. The conservative false-positive uncertainty before actual bytes is intentional. Database fencing cannot revoke a request already admitted to an external provider, so singleton is not an exactly-once effect guarantee.

independentChallenges.case: K1 is retry_wait or outcome_unknown, K2 is pending, and J1 has another key. Then resolve K1 to a known terminal outcome.
independentChallenges.assessment: K2 stays blocked while K1 is live or unknown; J1 may progress. Success, safe cancellation or proved-no-effect terminal failure releases K without deleting K1 evidence. A failed or expired worker cannot manufacture that release from uncertain effect state. Unsupported payload versions must remain held and cannot be silently skipped to authorize same-key overtaking.

independentChallenges.area: Immutable identity, due revision and late receipt
independentChallenges.case: Concurrent scans select revision A; patch A to B before admission or after admission; perform A-to-B-to-A due-value changes; deliver A's late receipt after B exists.
independentChallenges.assessment: Transactional uniqueness keeps one ID/payload for each revision, including terminal identities. Supplied due_at advances revision even when its value is unchanged. Admission rechecks revision, current owner/recipient/effect authority and visibility; completion marks only the matching current unsent revision. An unknown A blocks B dispatch but does not require discarding B's separate identity.

independentChallenges.case: Each invocation consumes the service's three allowed attempts, then fails safely; restart and next_schedule repeat. Separately crash after claim before outcome bookkeeping, or reclaim after the absolute intent deadline.
independentChallenges.assessment: The finite intent invocation count and first-claim absolute lifetime persist across restart/reclaim/schedules and bound the total invocations. Each invocation's service calls share their three-attempt/30-second budget. Admission/attempt accounting must be durable before execution so crashes cannot reset or evade either count. Expiry/exhaustion with no effect dead-letters; expiry after possible effect remains unknown. Numeric golden job limits are explicitly deferred to RM-108.
independentChallenges.disposition: sound_at_contract_level; crash accounting remains an executable gate

independentChallenges.case: Workers disagree on host wall time; a timezone/DST transition occurs; a safe database retry crosses a due-date/expiry boundary inside one job activation.
independentChallenges.assessment: Lease ownership uses authoritative database time; application timestamps and eligibility use compiler operation snapshots; scheduled_for is separate nominal data; active elapsed budgets use monotonic time; restart deadlines are absolute UTC instants checked on resumption. TIME-D05/TX-001 explicitly refresh the operation snapshot for a transaction retry, with nested calls sharing that attempt's snapshot. The candidate's unrefreshed scheduled_for wording does not override those incorporated retry semantics. Database lease time must not leak into domain timestamps or provider accepted_at into ordering authority.
independentChallenges.disposition: sound_at_contract_level; no distributed clock-synchronization or hard preemption claim

independentChallenges.case: Many ticks occur during downtime or a long run; a 501-row scan restarts after one bounded page; a due-date/visibility change occurs between pages.
independentChallenges.assessment: One active run and one pending follow-up bound tick backlog. Activations select at most 500 rows, persist keyset continuation and recheck current eligibility. Cursor advancement must not lose selected intents at a crash boundary. The stable-row candidate trace specifies no gaps/duplicate effects; changing eligibility must follow current authority rather than stale page payloads.
independentChallenges.disposition: sound_at_contract_level; cursor/enqueue atomicity and multiple scheduler processes require implementation evidence

independentChallenges.area: Cancellation, trusted resolution and operator replay
independentChallenges.case: Cancel before dispatch versus after possible_dispatch; resolve unknown with a trustworthy exact-intent receipt or no-effect proof; attempt replay after success, exhaustion or advancement of the same ordering key.
independentChallenges.assessment: Pre-effect cancellation stops dispatch; post-admission cancellation records a request without claiming rollback. Trusted acceptance resolves the original intent without another send. A resolved no-effect outcome may use only an already-declared safe retry with remaining budget. Privileged replay is not blanket permission to reopen success/permanent failure or violate FIFO after terminal key release. Replay preserves ID, payload, version and key; unresolved unknown and exhausted budgets remain prohibited.
independentChallenges.disposition: sound_at_contract_level under the existing safe-retry and FIFO constraints

independentChallenges.case: An authored job attempts to use retained intent state as a capability, dispatch to a changed unauthorized recipient, or invoke compiler maintenance purge; an age-based cleanup removes uniqueness evidence.
independentChallenges.assessment: Delivery state is compiler-private; SERVICE-001 admission rechecks current principal/effect/recipient authority. POLICY-D30 still governs authored jobs. Maintenance authority is separately clause-bound under POLICY-D30-M1 and cannot be acquired by an authored job. Terminal identity/evidence retention prevents duplicate same-revision enqueue after cleanup; no automatic purge is approved.
